Playing together online (games round a table in the games room, tag, snowball fights, the train and the slopes together, races), a profile card and the villager's own look, one villager across a phone, a laptop and a desktop, more than one villager on a device, real card tables, and Santa's sleigh in pixel art.

**Online, easier to find**
- **The ✉ friends button**, top right (✉ on a phone, in the web page's bar), with a dot for online and how many friends are about; it pulses when something's waiting.
- **The post** (what's happening online) sits bottom left on the desktop and top left on a phone or the web, clear of the clock and the joystick, and a click on it opens friends & online. A first-time hint says where online is.
- ✉ friends is first in ✦ things to do, and on the villager's own right-click menu.

**Playing together** (in a shared village: *☺ with the … here*, or a right-click on a friend)
- **Questions come up at the top of the screen**: *Sam asks: a game of chess?* **Y** yes, **N** no thanks (or a click). They're asked again now and then until answered, so one that goes astray isn't lost.
- **The games room.** Chess, checkers, Snowflakes or Twenty-One with a friend, or *round the table (everyone asked)* for up to four at the cards. Everyone goes to the games room in the host's home: in by the door, over to a chair at the long table under the lamp (one at each end, two behind it), a chair pulled out, sat down, everyone in their own chair for everyone else to see. The one who asked deals, and deals again; at Twenty-One the deal passes round. Moves go to everyone at the table and are sent again until they're taken in. Walking out leaves the table; at the cards the others play on.
- **Tag** with a friend (a ⚑ over whoever's it), **snowball fights** (hits counted both ways), **waves, hearts and cheers**.
- **Light shows, fireworks and carols** happen for everyone in the shared village.
- **The train and the slopes together.** Off up the mountain, everyone's asked along: a yes puts them on the same shuttle or train (walking the carriage and sitting in the seats, names over them) or up at the lodge; a friend away on a trip can be joined where they are. Friends ski down alongside, in the standings. **Races**: everyone asked, up the chairlift together, down the same course, the results at the bottom.

**Profiles**
- **The villager's own look**: Settings → You → *your look* (coat, hat, hair, skin, a scarf; *classic* is the old green hat and gold coat), on the phone and the web too. Friends online see it.
- **The profile card**: the look, a line about the villager (*card's line*), the pet, games and fights won, runs and the best score down the mountain, cheer, friends. *★ my profile card*; a friend's from their name.
- **One villager on all your devices.** *✉ friends → my devices → link another device* shows a link code; typed on the other device, it becomes the same villager (the same village, name, look, pet, friends & family, friend code and friends; what it had done is added in). From then on they keep in step through the relay: what each does adds up (even both played at once: cheer earned on one and spent on the other comes out right), and a change to the villager or the village on one shows on the others. Each device's side is kept by the relay, so one that's been off catches up.
- **More than one villager on a device**: *villagers on this device → a new villager*, each with their own village, look and friends; *switch to …* brings one back.

**The table games**
- **A real deck on the table**: the cards slide off it to each hand; the dealer's hidden card turns over at the end.
- **Up to four at the cards**: Snowflakes and Twenty-One with up to three of the household (or friends online).
- **Twenty-One: the deal passes on** (**P**, or *pass the deal*). A neighbour dealing keeps to the house rule; dealing yourself, you play last and choose.
- **Clicks only play what they're on**: the board, a card, the deck, or the buttons under the game (*hit*, *stand*, *draw a card*, *again*). A click to bring the window forward no longer hits.
- **Sat down to play**: the villager and whoever's playing sit at the table.
- **On autopilot**, the villager now and then knocks at a neighbour's door for a game, plays it out, shakes hands and heads off.

**Fixes and looks**
- **Santa's sleigh and reindeer** are pixel art like everyone else: four reindeer in red harness with bells, Rudolph's nose glowing, Santa in a gold-trimmed sleigh with a sack of presents.
- **A menu over someone no longer makes them vanish**: just the part under it is hidden.
- **Friends brought home are visitors**: they say how cosy it is, not "come in, you have to see our tree"; only the household welcomes the villager.
- Changing a scene setting on the desktop no longer drops the friends list and friend code (the village made anew keeps them).
